content:
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud & Infrastructure Engineer
Rotterdam, Netherlands | samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud and infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing, building and operating Azure environments. Focused on Terraform-based infrastructure, cloud networking, Azure operations and deployment automation. Experienced in managing large Windows and Linux server estates, supporting AKS operations and delivering infrastructure changes in production environments.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud: Microsoft Azure (VMs, VNets, App Service, AKS, Azure Migrate, Azure Monitor)
Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, Bicep; Terratest module tests
Cloud operations: Azure DevOps YAML pipelines, Kubernetes (AKS), Docker, Helm, Ansible
Networking and security: Hub-spoke networks, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints, VNet peering, TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, MFA, Conditional Access
Systems and automation: Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), Active Directory / Entra ID, Microsoft 365 administration, PowerShell, Bash

EXPERIENCE
Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V., Rotterdam
Mar 2025 – Present
- Part of a three-person cloud team operating an Azure estate of approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters across three subscriptions.
- Built Terraform modules for hub-spoke landing-zone networking, including Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering across subscriptions.
- Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and implemented a nightly infrastructure drift-detection job.
- Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines for build, test and deployment to App Service or AKS. Deployment frequency increased from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.
- Operate AKS clusters, including upgrades, node pools and ingress; application manifests are owned by the development teams.

Freelance IT Administrator | Self-employed, small businesses
Sep 2022 – Jan 2024
- Set up and supported Microsoft 365 and Azure AD for nine small businesses with 5–40 employees.
- Migrated two clients from on-premises file servers to SharePoint and OneDrive.
- Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for security baselines, including MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing and backups.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, Schiedam
Jan 2014 – Feb 2020
- Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting municipal services.
- Led the lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate. Cutover was completed over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
- Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.
- Served as second-line escalation for network and Active Directory issues.

Helpdesk Technician | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Aug 2011 – Dec 2013

CAREER BREAKS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Mar 2020 – Aug 2022 | Full-time family caregiving; maintained Azure Administrator knowledge and provided unpaid IT support to church and family.
Feb 2024 – Feb 2025 | Completed a part-time, online, three-month English-language cloud bootcamp (Dec 2024); studied Terraform and built a Proxmox homelab.

EDUCATION
MBO 4 IT Systems and Networks | Delta Vocational College, 2011

CERTIFICATIONS
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), 2019
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003), 2025

LANGUAGES
Dutch (native) | English (fluent) | Twi (spoken)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with a clear cloud/infrastructure positioning and credible quantified achievements. The Havenstad experience is particularly effective: it demonstrates scale, production operations, Terraform delivery, Kubernetes operations, automation, and measurable deployment improvement. The migration achievement also provides strong evidence of ownership and reliability. Career breaks are explained professionally without overexplaining them. The main content limitation is that the CV does not explicitly frame the candidate's existing work in the job's terms of systems architecture, system design, and leading technical topics. It also does not distinguish clearly between independently owned work and team-owned work beyond the useful AKS clarification.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, simple text formatting, chronological experience, searchable technology names, and no problematic tables, graphics, columns, headers, or footers. Relevant terms such as Azure, Terraform, Kubernetes, AKS, Docker, Helm, Azure DevOps, networking, security, Windows, Linux, and virtual machines are present. AI/ATS screening probability is high for Azure-focused infrastructure and DevOps roles, but only moderate for this specific vacancy because exact terms such as Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, systems architecture, system design, and stakeholder engagement are not present. These are genuine capability gaps or unsupported areas in the supplied candidate information, so they should not be added merely as keywords.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with hands-on infrastructure engineering, Azure cloud environment design and operation, Terraform, Linux and virtual machines, practical security, and production platform operations. It also provides credible evidence of leading technical delivery through the 60-server Azure migration and ownership of landing-zone networking and deployment automation. The Azure background is acceptable under the ad's allowance for other major clouds, although AWS is preferred. The candidate's material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS implementation, IoT/automotive or remote-device integration, JVM/backend development, or explicit experience negotiating interfaces with external manufacturers and bringing stakeholders along. These are gaps in the candidate material rather than CV-writing defects. The CV does show adjacent experience relevant to the role's engineering-led and ownership-oriented environment: landing-zone design, platform reliability, secure networking, observability through Azure Monitor, drift detection, and operational ownership of Azure and AKS.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, change the second sentence to explicitly use the supported architecture terms: "Focused on Terraform-based infrastructure, cloud networking, systems architecture, cloud environment design and operation, and deployment automation." This accurately reflects the hub-spoke landing-zone design, Azure operations, and production automation already documented.
2. In the Cloud Engineer experience section under Havenstad Logistics, revise the Terraform bullet to begin with the design responsibility: "Designed and built Terraform modules for hub-spoke landing-zone networking..." This makes the existing systems-design evidence more visible to recruiters and ATS screening without claiming unsupported Terragrunt or mTLS experience.
3. In the same Havenstad section, revise the AKS bullet to make operational ownership and team boundaries more direct: "Operate AKS clusters in production, including upgrades, node pools and ingress; development teams own application manifests." This is clearer and more concise while preserving the important scope limitation.
4. In the Systems Administrator section, revise the migration bullet to foreground technical leadership: "Led the technical delivery of a lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; completed cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime." This strengthens alignment with the requirement to lead technical topics using an achievement already supported by the original information.
5. In the Core Skills section, consider changing the heading "Networking and security" to "Networking, security and access" and retain the existing supported terms, including TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, MFA and Conditional Access. Do not add mTLS, SSL/TLS, or certificate management unless the candidate can substantiate that experience.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "delivering infrastructure changes in production environments"

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, and professionally written. It presents strong evidence of Azure infrastructure engineering through concrete scale, technologies, and outcomes: approximately 400 VMs, 12 AKS clusters, 15 application pipelines, and a 60-server migration completed without unplanned downtime. The use of metrics and project-level detail gives the document credibility. The career breaks are explained transparently and professionally. The main content weaknesses are that some listed technologies are not supported by the Original Candidate Information, while several relevant supported details—such as Azure Migrate, site-to-site VPN, and technical delivery leadership—could be used more strategically. Evidence of stakeholder engagement, system design decision-making, and secure communications is limited.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience, searchable technology keywords, and no problematic tables, graphics, or text columns. Keyword coverage is strong for Azure, Terraform, Kubernetes, AKS, networking, security, Linux, virtual machines, and Azure DevOps. AI and ATS screening probability is good, approximately 85%, for Azure-focused infrastructure roles. Screening performance for this particular role is reduced by the absence of Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, and explicit stakeholder/system-design language. Unsupported skills in the Core Skills section also create a truthfulness and screening-risk issue and should be removed.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a strong match for hands-on infrastructure engineering, Azure cloud environment design and operation, Terraform, systems administration, Linux, virtual machines, practical security, and technical delivery. The Azure landing-zone work, AKS operations, pipeline automation, and VMware-to-Azure migration align well with Corvale's engineering-led and ownership-oriented environment. The candidate has credible evidence of leading technical delivery through the 60-server migration and designing reusable infrastructure modules. However, the candidate's material does not demonstrate Terragrunt, AWS, mTLS or SSL/TLS, IoT/automotive or remote-device integration, or JVM/backend development. Stakeholder engagement and challenging system-design decisions are also not explicitly evidenced. These are capability gaps or evidence limitations in the candidate material, not defects that can be fixed merely by rewriting the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES
1. In the Core Skills section under “Infrastructure as Code,” remove “Bicep” because it is not supported by the Original Candidate Information. Retain “Terraform” and “Terratest module tests.”
2. In the Core Skills section under “Cloud,” remove “Azure Monitor” because it is not supported by the Original Candidate Information. Do not replace it with another monitoring tool.
3. In the Core Skills section under “Cloud operations,” remove “Ansible” because it is not supported by the Original Candidate Information. Retain Azure DevOps YAML pipelines, Kubernetes (AKS), Docker, and Helm.

HIGH-VALUE, TRUTHFUL ENHANCEMENTS
4. In the Professional Summary, make the strongest job-relevant evidence more explicit without claiming unsupported experience. For example, change the final sentence to: “Experienced in operating large Windows and Linux server estates, leading infrastructure delivery, automating deployments, and supporting AKS operations.” This is supported by the 250-server estate, the 60-server migration, the 15 application pipelines, and the AKS responsibilities.
5. In the Experience section under “Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services,” revise the migration bullet to include the supported architecture and networking terms: “Led the technical delivery of a lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate, Azure VMs, VNets and site-to-site VPN; completed cutover over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.”
6. In the Experience section under “Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V.,” change “Designed and built Terraform modules for hub-spoke landing-zone networking” to “Designed and built reusable Terraform modules for hub-spoke landing-zone networking.” This better highlights maintainable infrastructure-as-code without claiming Terragrunt experience.
7. In the same Havenstad experience section, retain the existing AKS clarification but make ownership boundaries especially clear: “Operate AKS clusters in production, including upgrades, node pools and ingress; development teams own application manifests.” This accurately demonstrates platform operations while avoiding an unsupported claim of application-development ownership.
8. In the Skills section, add “Azure Migrate” and “site-to-site VPN” to the relevant Azure/networking lists because both are supported by the candidate portfolio and improve alignment with infrastructure migration and networking requirements. Do not add mTLS, SSL/TLS, Terragrunt, AWS, IoT, or JVM keywords.

Potential unsupported skills/hallucinations were identified in the generated CV: “Bicep,” “Azure Monitor,” and “Ansible” appear in Core Skills but are not present in the Original Candidate Information. These must be removed unless independently verified by the candidate. The corresponding fixes are specified in improvement instructions 1–3.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professionally structured CV with a clear Azure infrastructure focus, relevant certifications, credible scale indicators, and measurable delivery outcomes. The strongest evidence includes operating approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters, designing reusable Terraform modules, automating deployments for 15 applications, and completing a 60-server Azure migration with no unplanned downtime. The career breaks are disclosed transparently and professionally. Content is concise and avoids unsupported claims; no potential hallucinations were detected against the Original Candidate Information. The main content limitation is that stakeholder engagement, system-design decision-making, and communication outcomes are not explicitly evidenced.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, readable text, standard date formats, searchable technology names, and no problematic tables, graphics, headers, or footers. It should parse well and has a high AI-screening probability for Azure-focused cloud infrastructure roles. Keyword coverage is strong for Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, AKS, Kubernetes, networking, Windows/Linux, security, and infrastructure operations. Screening probability for this specific vacancy is somewhat lower because the document does not contain Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, IoT, or explicit stakeholder/system-design terminology. These are largely candidate-profile gaps rather than formatting defects, because the Original Candidate Information does not substantiate those technologies or experiences.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with the core infrastructure, cloud environment design and operation, Terraform, networking, security, Linux, and virtual-machine aspects of the role. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background because the advertisement states that AWS is preferred rather than mandatory. The landing-zone networking project and AKS/App Service deployment work are particularly relevant to Corvale's platform-infrastructure scope. The CV also demonstrates technical ownership through the Azure migration, Terraform module development, drift detection, and release-pipeline automation. However, the candidate material does not show Terragrunt, AWS, mTLS or SSL/TLS implementation, certificate management, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, JVM development, or explicit experience aligning stakeholders such as manufacturers' engineers. The document also does not directly demonstrate observability design, telemetry ingestion, video streaming, or remote-device connectivity. These are genuine alignment gaps, not defects that can be fixed through rewriting. The contractor background is relevant, but the CV could make technical leadership and system-design thinking more explicit using evidence already available.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, TARGETED IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, revise the final sentence to make the architecture and technical-leadership evidence more explicit without adding unsupported claims. For example, change "Experienced in operating large Windows and Linux server estates, leading infrastructure delivery, automating deployments, and supporting AKS operations" to "Experienced in operating large Windows and Linux server estates, leading infrastructure delivery and Azure migration work, designing landing-zone networking, automating deployments, and supporting AKS operations."
2. In the Cloud Engineer experience section under Havenstad Logistics, revise the Terraform bullet to include the system-design terminology supported by the work. For example, change "Designed and built reusable Terraform modules for hub-spoke landing-zone networking" to "Designed and built reusable Terraform modules for hub-spoke landing-zone networking and Azure cloud environment architecture." Keep the existing technical details about Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints, and VNet peering.
3. In the Systems Administrator section under Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, make the leadership outcome more prominent by changing "Led the technical delivery of a lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS" to "Led the technical delivery and cutover planning for a lift-and-shift migration of 60 VMware servers to Azure IaaS." This remains supported by the Original Candidate Information and better matches the requirement for leading technical topics.
4. In the Career Breaks and Professional Development section, improve the bootcamp wording for chronological clarity. Change "Completed a part-time, online, three-month English-language cloud bootcamp (Dec 2024)" to "Completed a three-month, part-time, online, English-language cloud bootcamp in December 2024."
